en: The Ritual Manual for the Dhāraṇī of the Gateways of Boundless Emanation Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by Amoghavajra;
the mantras are as in the sūtra.
By practicing this, one gives rise to the turning of the three types of activity through the gate of the infinite *dhāraṇī*.
Relying upon the three gates of secrecy—namely, the three vajras:
the body seal (*mudrā*), speech mantra (*mantra*), and [mind samādhi]—one proceeds.
The mind abides in samādhi through the well-established yoga of entering the three equalities;
by means of one’s own body being identical to the deity,
one attains perfect enlightenment even while an ordinary being— this method is most profound and secret.
As stated in the King of the Mahāvairocana Sūtra:
"Even those such as those in their final birth before Buddhahood do not possess its sphere; how much less so those of inferior wisdom?
Like obtaining the jewel of a Wheel-Turning King, one should keep it secret and not speak of it recklessly."
This Honored One is Karmaprajñāpāramitā;
because she arises from abiding [in that state], she manifests in the form of a youthful maiden to reveal herself as the Great Compassionate Mother. All Buddhas abide in this wisdom.
Able to universally manifest the form-body,
seated upon a lotus throne in the full-lotus posture with the mind of great bodhicitta,
his majestic bearing of the Great Seal is identical to that of Amoghasiddhi, possessing the physical characteristics of a Tathāgata.
The Samādhi-Wing forms the Vajra-Fist; holding a lotus at the heart, it places the Prajñā-pāramitā scripture.
The Wisdom-Wing displays the gesture of preaching the Dharma, with palms raised and the five fingers extended. The Peak of Patience manifests Karma.
The ten-spoked vajra wheel adorns his crown, with the five Tathāgatas upon it;
his entire body is the color of green grass.
Furthermore, the syllable *ba* resides in his limbs, while the syllable *la* is situated at his heart, forming the ūrṇā-kośa (the hair-treasure between the eyebrows).
The syllable *vaṃ* is placed at the tip of the tongue;
the syllable *ja* is placed on the head, green in color, forming the uṣṇīṣa-mudrā.
The syllable *ka* is placed in the palm of wisdom, its color forming the karma-mudrā—the wheel of the twelve links of dependent origination.
The yellow syllable *Dha* is placed in the palms joined in meditative equipoise, forming a lotus flower with the Prajñā fingers;
the syllable *Śa* is placed upon the feet of Avalokiteśvara. The syllable *Kṣa* is placed on the soles of the feet;
these five syllables are all brilliant white, like snow, milk, a swan, or the moon.
These syllables form the wheel-sign;
this is the empowerment of the *samaya* secret mudrā at the crown of the head.
The sequence of the initial and final rites is identical to the ritual manuals (*vidhi*) of all the families (*kula*). [This is the teaching] of eighty *koṭi* Buddhas.
They surround this Honored One and dwell there; furthermore,
eight bodhisattvas abide in the eight directions, along with eight yakṣas, the four means of attraction,
and the eight offerings, all arranged in successive order.
The Secret Maṇḍala: A Recitation Manual for the Sūtra of Mantras, Compiled according to the Original Teachings;
a Revised Edition of the Fundamental Ritual Procedures for Practice. Honored Teaching.
